positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
- Develop and maintain enterprise web based applications in Scala using Play Framework
-  Work environment: Agile/Scrum
- Tech Stack: Scala (Play, SBT, Cats), SQL (PostgreSQL), Redis, JavaScript (Backbone.js, Underscore.js, React, jQuery, AJAX, Webpack), HTML, Bootstrap, JSON, XML, REST, GitHub, CircleCI, AWS, JIRA, Confluence, Monday.com

positions.title: Software Quality Assurance Engineer
positions.description:
- Review product design documentation to ensure that requirements stated are correct, unambiguous, and verifiable.
- Consult with product development to evaluate system interfaces, operational requirements, and performance requirements of overall system.
- Define test methods and create test plans for new or updated software projects to determine if the software will perform accurately and reliably according to documented requirements as well as established standards under both normal and abnormal conditions.
- Execute test plans and create test reports to describe program evaluation, testing, and correction.

positions.title: Manual QA
positions.description:
• Responsible for running existing manual test scripts for various applications. 
• Enhancement of existing manual tests and create new test scripts
• Manually execute steps in test cases when necessary.
• Organize and report results out of our test management software.
• Create documentation for QA Team as needed (best practices, run instructions, etc.).

projects.title: Variable speed Motor Control
projects.description:
•Design, code, test and demonstrate a variable speed motor control using a PIC trainer board.
•Use C language to code all commands on Microsoft visual studio and MPLAB.

projects.title: Accumulator
projects.description:
•Constructed a 4-bit accumulator with a 7-dip switch on Quartus II that required four switches for data input, 1 switch for Load, 1 switch for Clear, and 1 switch for Transfer. 
•Connected design to Altera DE2 board and test its basic functionality by loading a 0001 into the accumulator then transferring the data several times.
